## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect should be fixed before merge. The new `status()` shortens the revision differently from the existing `history()` and `completed()` output, even though its docstring says it uses the same identifier. The added tests don't check the revision part of the status line, so they pass anyway.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — `status()` uses `short_revision = revision[:7]`, but its docstring at line 13 says "Show the deployment revision using the same identifier as history", and `history()`/`completed()` use `revision[:12]` (lines 5 and 9). With the test fixture `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef..."`, `status()` returns `"Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)"` while `history()` returns `"History: 0123456789ab"`. Could you change line 14 to `revision[:12]` and make `test_running_status_contains_attempt` assert the full string `"Running: 0123456789ab (attempt 2)"` instead of only `startswith`/`endswith`? — A running deployment's status line shows a different revision ID from its history and completion lines, so operators can't match them by string, and the 7-character prefix is more likely to clash with another revision. The current tests can't catch this.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `attempt_label()` is tested for exact output on more than one input (`tests/test_display.py:18-22`).
